title: Checkpoint: Getting Started
intro: Check that you can run Python, print text, and read the first error messages you will meet.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: sep sets what goes between the values, so print puts a dash instead of the usual space.

questions.question: What happens when you run this line?
questions.explanation: Python is case-sensitive. Only print exists, so Print is an unknown name and raises NameError.

questions.question: You see >>> in your window, type python hello.py and get a SyntaxError. What is wrong?
options: The file hello.py is empty, so there is nothing to run
You are in the Python REPL: type exit(), then run it in the terminal
You must write print(python hello.py) to run a file
Python is not installed, so the command is not known
questions.explanation: The >>> prompt means you are already inside Python, where only Python code works. Terminal commands belong at the $ or PS prompt.

questions.question: A script file contains only the line below. You run it with python3 sum.py. What do you see?
questions.explanation: Scripts do not show values automatically like the REPL does. Wrap the expression in print() to see it.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: end="!" replaces the usual newline with !, so the next print continues on the same line.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: The part in quotes is text and is printed as-is; the part without quotes is calculated. print adds a space between them.

questions.question: Which comment is the most useful?
questions.explanation: Good comments explain why or give context the code cannot show. The others just repeat what the code already says.

questions.question: Why does this program fail?
options: print needs a colon at the end
The second line is indented for no reason
questions.explanation: Only code inside a block (like the body of an if) should be indented. The extra spaces cause IndentationError: unexpected indent.

questions.question: Which command opens the interactive Python shell (the REPL) in a terminal on macOS or Linux?
questions.explanation: python3 with no file name starts the REPL, where you see the >>> prompt. python3 hello.py runs a file instead.

questions.question: In the REPL you type the line below and press Enter. Nothing appears. Why?
options: An assignment has no value to show; the REPL only echoes expressions
Python is still waiting for a second line of input
The variable name total is reserved and was ignored
The REPL never shows anything until you call print()
questions.explanation: The REPL shows the value of an expression such as total or 2 + 3, but an assignment produces no value, so nothing is shown.
